text: A resume should contain reliable contact information.
A concise professional summary helps quickly explain the candidate's profile.
Experience bullets should begin with action verbs and describe concrete contributions.
Strong achievement bullets include measurable outcomes such as percentages, time, revenue, scale, or volume.
A clear skills section should contain technologies and competencies relevant to the target role.
A targeted resume should reflect important skills from the job description when they are genuinely supported.
A cover letter should connect verified candidate evidence to the target role without repeating the entire resume or inventing qualifications.
Projects are useful evidence of practical ability, especially for students and early-career candidates.
Use a professional email address and include a working phone number or portfolio link when relevant to the role.
Tailor the opening summary to the target position by emphasizing relevant experience and skills already supported elsewhere in the resume.
Lead each experience bullet with a precise action verb and explain the scope, method, or outcome of the work.
Prefer concise accomplishment statements over generic duty lists; preserve the candidate's original facts when editing.
When accurate figures are available, quantify results with percentages, time saved, scale, volume, quality, or cost; never invent metrics.
Group technical tools and role-relevant competencies into a concise skills section and remove unsupported or irrelevant claims.
Use the job description's exact terminology where it accurately describes existing experience; do not add a keyword as a claimed skill without evidence.
Prioritize required qualifications and recurring role-specific terms over copying every phrase from a job posting.
Open with the target role and a specific reason grounded in the candidate's documented experience, then connect one or two relevant achievements to the employer's needs.
Keep a cover letter concise, professional, and specific; avoid generic claims, unsupported motivation, and repeating the full resume.
Describe a relevant project with its purpose, the candidate's contribution, and the technologies or outcomes explicitly stated in the source.
Use a simple, consistent, single-column layout with clear section headings and standard text to improve machine parsing.
Avoid placing essential contact details in headers, footers, text boxes, images, or complex tables because some applicant tracking systems may not extract them reliably.
Keep bullets focused and scannable, use consistent tense and punctuation, and remove redundant wording.
Use conventional labels for sections such as Experience, Education, Skills, and Projects so resume parsers and readers can identify them.
